label: Peplink MAX BR1 IP55 Outdoor
description: Outdoor IP55 LTE router: 1x GE WAN, 2x GE LAN, 100 Mbps throughput, Wi-Fi, PoE in.
notes: Vendor figures from the Peplink tech-spec sheet: Ethernet WAN port 1 (GE), Number of Ethernet LAN port 2 (GE), Router Throughput **100 Mbps**, Wi-Fi AP Yes, PoE Input Yes. **Gigabit ports, 100 Mbps router** - the copper speed suggests ten times the throughput the box can actually forward, which is the single most misleading pairing in this whole vendor's range. **PoE: the WAN port is the inlet.** The tech-spec sheet prints `PoE Input PoE: DC 48-56V` / `Yes [2]` with `[2] 802.3at PoE+ or 56V Peplink Passive PoE` and `Maximum Power Consumption 18W (w/o PoE)`, which gives the class and the draw but not the socket; the product datasheet's panel does - `1x 10/100/1000M Ethernet WAN (PoE Input)` next to `2x 10/100/1000M Ethernet LAN (LAN1 - 802.3at PoE Output)`. So `wan1` declares `poeIn: 18` (the sheet maximum, what a PSE has to fund) and LAN 1 / LAN 2 declare `poeIn: false` - neither is an inlet. LAN 1 is the reverse direction: an optional 802.3at PoE+ **output** that needs the separately sold PoE injector (ACW-107) and, for the full 25.5 W, a 56 V input; it is documented here and deliberately not modelled as a PSE, because this row is a correction of the PD side only. Sources: https://www.peplink.com/compare/tech-specs/br1-ip55.pdf and https://download.peplink.com/resources/pepwave_max_br_ip55_datasheet.pdf.
